rewrite_brief: Use when console logging isn't enough for a Node.js issue — need real breakpoints, stepping, scope/stack inspection, or CPU/heap profiling.; Two approaches: the zero-install built-in CLI debugger for quick interactive poking, or a scriptable remote-debugging-protocol client for automating breakpoints or capturing state non-interactively.; Covers launching paused at start, attaching to an already-running process via a signal-triggered inspector, TypeScript sourcemap caveats, propagating the inspector into child processes, and scripting CPU-profile/heap-snapshot capture.; Pitfalls: breakpoints hit compiled JS rather than TypeScript source unless sourcemaps are followed; starting without a pause-on-entry flag lets execution race past early breakpoints; multiple debugged processes collide on the default port; a parent's inspector flag doesn't propagate to children; interactive stepping needs a PTY-capable terminal; never expose the inspector on a non-local network interface.; Verification: confirm exactly the intended process appears in the target list, confirm the first breakpoint actually halts execution, confirm the paused location matches expectations.

one_line_summary: Runs a pre-commit verification pipeline — static security scan, baseline-aware tests/lint, and an independent reviewer sub-agent with an auto-fix loop — before code is committed.
depends_on: git, the project's own test framework and linters (auto-detected per language), a multi-agent task-delegation capability for the independent reviewer and fixer roles

rewrite_brief: Use after implementing a change and before commit/push, especially when the user signals readiness to ship; skip for docs-only or trivial config edits.; Pull the diff, run pattern-based static scans for hardcoded secrets, injection risks, unsafe eval/exec, and unsafe deserialization, and run tests/linters compared against a pre-change baseline so only newly introduced failures count as blocking.; Hand the diff plus scan results — and nothing else — to a separate reviewer role with no shared context, instructed to fail closed on any finding or an unparseable diff.; On failure, dispatch a third, narrowly scoped fixer role that addresses only the listed issues, then re-run the whole pipeline, capping the loop at two rounds before escalating to the user.; Only commit once everything passes, marking the commit as independently reviewed.; Pitfalls: split oversized diffs by file; treat missing tooling/empty diffs as skip-not-fail; treat unparseable reviewer output as automatic failure; watch for the auto-fix loop introducing new regressions.

one_line_summary: Fans out four parallel, narrowly focused reviewers (reuse, quality, efficiency, architectural altitude) over a diff and applies the resulting cleanup fixes by risk tier.

rewrite_brief: Use only when explicitly asked to clean up/simplify recently changed code — a quality pass, not a correctness bug hunt — and never run automatically after routine edits.; Capture the relevant diff; if parallel delegation isn't available, work through the same four review angles sequentially instead of skipping coverage.; Run four reviewers concurrently: duplicated logic that should reuse existing utilities; general code-quality smells; efficiency issues (wasted work, missed concurrency, leaks, swallowed errors); and band-aid fixes applied at the wrong layer instead of the shared root cause — each required to cite concrete evidence and a confidence/risk rating.; Merge and deduplicate findings, resolve conflicts favoring correctness and the user's stated focus, then apply fixes in risk order: low-risk automatically, medium-risk one file at a time with test verification, high-risk flagged for human decision only.; Pitfalls: don't exceed four reviewers or split the diff between them; verify apparent 'band-aids' against version history before flagging as removable since some are deliberate compatibility shims.; Verification: re-run affected tests/linters after each fix, revert anything that breaks, summarize applied changes by category/risk tier.

one_line_summary: Enforces a four-phase root-cause-first debugging discipline — build a red/green repro loop, analyze patterns, test ranked hypotheses, then fix once — before any code change is allowed.
depends_on: terminal (to run tests/repros), git, code-search/file-read tooling, optional multi-agent delegation for investigation-only sub-tasks
hermes_coupling: search_files/read_file/terminal/web_search/web_extract/delegate_task tool names, cross-references to companion TDD and subagent-workflow skills
suggested_use: DEFAULT — a pure, widely applicable debugging methodology with minimal platform-specific coupling.
rewrite_brief: Use for any technical bug, regression, performance issue, or build failure, especially under time pressure, to resist patching before understanding the cause.; Phase 1: read errors fully, build or find a tight, fast, deterministic reproduction; check recent changes; add boundary instrumentation to localize failure in multi-component systems.; Phase 2: shrink the reproduction to its minimal form one variable at a time, diff against a working/reference example to enumerate every difference.; Phase 3: generate several ranked, falsifiable hypotheses with explicit predictions, test only the top-ranked one with the smallest possible change, avoid stacking untested fixes.; Phase 4: write a regression test that reproduces the bug before fixing it, apply one root-cause fix at a time, verify against the full suite, apply a 'rule of three' — after three failed attempts, stop and question the underlying design.; Verification is the reproduction loop flipping from red to green plus a clean full-suite run with no new failures.

one_line_summary: Enforces strict test-first Red-Green-Refactor development, one small vertical behavior slice at a time, with no production code written ahead of its test.
depends_on: the project's test runner (executed via a terminal tool), optional multi-agent delegation to enforce TDD discipline in dispatched implementation work
hermes_coupling: terminal tool invocation examples, delegate_task tool for enforcing TDD in a dispatched sub-task, cross-reference to a companion systematic-debugging skill
suggested_use: DEFAULT — TDD is a universal, foundational software practice with essentially no platform-specific dependency.
rewrite_brief: Use for nearly all production code work with narrow, user-approved exceptions for throwaway prototypes, generated code, or plain config files.; Red: write one small test for a single behavior and actually run it to confirm it fails for the right reason before writing any implementation.; Green: write the minimal code needed to pass that one test — hardcoding or duplicating logic at this stage is acceptable and deferred.; Refactor: only once green, clean up duplication/naming/structure without changing behavior, re-running tests continuously and reverting immediately if a refactor breaks anything.; Explicitly rejects writing a batch of tests followed by a batch of implementation in favor of one vertical slice at a time, and treats production code written before its failing test as a violation requiring deletion and redo.; Verification checklist: every new function has a test, each test was observed failing for the right reason first, the full suite passes cleanly afterward, mocks are used only when a real dependency genuinely can't be exercised.
